reason: The passage describes the people as passive recipients of divine deliverance rather than active collaborators with their leaders. When the people cry out in fear and complain to Moses about being taken out of Egypt to die, Moses does not invite them into collaborative action. Instead, he instructs them: 'Do not be afraid. Stand firm... The Lord will fight for you; you need only to be still' (וְאַתֶּם תַּחֲרִישׁוּן - 'you be silent/still'). The active agents are God (who fights, parts the sea, and confuses the Egyptian camp) and Moses (who stretches his hand over the sea), while the people are explicitly told to remain inactive. The narrative shows no evidence of leaders and people working together toward a shared goal; rather, it shows the people in a dependent, passive role while their leader and God act on their behalf.
